title: LIBERO-Para: A Diagnostic Benchmark and Metrics for Paraphrase Robustness in VLA Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.28301v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models achieve strong performance in robotic manipulation by leveraging pre-trained vision-language backbones. However, in downstream robotic settings, they are typically fine-tuned with limited data, leading to overfitting to specific instruction formulations and leaving robustness to paraphrased instructions underexplored. To study this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Para, a controlled benchmark that independently varies action expressions and object references for fine-grained analysis of linguistic generalization. Across seven VLA configurations (0.6B-7.5B), we observe consistent performance degradation of 22-52 pp under paraphrasing. This degradation is primarily driven by object-level lexical variation: even simple synonym substitutions cause large drops, indicating reliance on surface-level matching rather than semantic grounding. translated_title: LIBERO-Para：用于评估VLA模型改述鲁棒性的诊断基准与指标
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作模型通过利用预训练的视觉-语言骨干网络，在机器人操作任务中取得了出色的性能。然而，在下游机器人应用场景中，这些模型通常使用有限的数据进行微调，导致其对特定指令表述过拟合，而对改述指令的鲁棒性尚未得到充分研究。为研究这一差距，我们提出了LIBERO-Para，一个受控基准，它独立地变化动作表达和对象指称，以实现对语言泛化能力的细粒度分析。在七种VLA配置（0.6B-7.5B）上，我们观察到改述条件下22-52个百分点的持续性能下降。这种下降主要由对象层面的词汇变化驱动：即使是简单的同义词替换也会导致大幅性能下滑，表明模型依赖于表面层面的匹配而非语义理解。此外，80-96%的失败源于规划层面的轨迹偏离……
tldr: 该论文提出了LIBERO-Para诊断基准与指标，通过独立变化动作表达和对象指称来系统评估VLA模型的改述鲁棒性，发现七种VLA配置在改述指令下性能下降22-52个百分点，且主要由对象层面的同义词变化引起，表明现有模型依赖表面词汇匹配而非真正的语义理解。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces LIBERO-Para, a controlled diagnostic benchmark and metrics that independently vary action expressions and object references, revealing consistent 22-52 pp performance degradation across seven VLA configurations under paraphrasing, primarily driven by object-level lexical variation such as simple synonym substitutions, indicating that VLA models rely on surface-level matching rather than semantic grounding.
